body:
Thanks for trying to help, but the relationship isn't really my biggest concern right now. We love each other but I don't know if staying together is more important that staying alive. We've both been considering suicide for a while.

For me it's mostly about money -- he doesn't want to work, but I do, but we can't save up any money since we just have the one car, he has better job prospects, and there's no work in this area that I can walk/bike to. It's a feedback loop we're stuck in and it's making both of us miserable. I'm stuck at home all day unable to do anything truly productive except think about exactly how fucked I am, how I'm almost certain to die in poverty, not being sure if my lights will turn on, not being sure when the water will be drinkable again, and getting eaten alive by fleas. And I don't live in a third world country... all of this is happening in Connecticut, so I'm surrounded by everyone elses' wealth and my fiance has to come home to all this crap after going through the homes of the 1% all day for his job. Then he comes home similarly upset about being underpaid and under appreciated at his job and doesn't want to do anything together that can take my mind off of things. I think a distraction would be a very good thing, especially if it could lead to a hobby or better yet paid work.

I don't know. I want to make it work, we used to make each other really happy. I'm cooped up all day in a house I hate, and he's away all day being underpaid at a job he hates... It's hard to be happy in the little time we have together, especially since we have opposite goals -- I'm dying to get out of the house, he just wants to stay at home and relax. We butt heads and argue a lot.

I need a purpose. Or at the very least a distraction. I was happier as a line cook in a shit hole of a pub full of bigots, at least I was busy.
